speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: As a parent of young children, I feel these issues acutely.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Their voices warn of a serious problem: the quiet extinction of diversity in our preschools.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Many young parents may have read in CNA of a spate of preschool closures over the last few years – at least six reported in the past two years alone.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: In 2013, the Early Childhood Development Agency (ECDA) was formed under the Ministry of Social and Family Development (MSF) to raise preschool standards.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Under it, two major schemes now dominate the sector.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Five large, Government-supported operators: PCF Sparkletots, NTUC My First Skool, E-Bridge, Skool4Kidz, and M.Y World.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: They receive significant grant funding and priority HDB site allocation, in exchange for capping fees and meeting quality requirements.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: These are mid-sized players with slightly higher fee caps but similar obligations.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Together, these two schemes have grown at a staggering rate.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: PCF and NTUC My First Skool alone account for at least 30% of all preschools.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: There is another angle of competition, coming directly from the Ministry of Education (MOE).

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: MOE Kindergartens (MKs) were launched in 2014 and are co-located within primary schools.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: A major draw for parents is priority under Phase 2A of Primary 1 registration for the primary school which creates a "through-train" for Primary 1 admission.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: You may know some of these primary schools: Temasek, Princess Elizabeth, Gongshang.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: This has pulled students away from independent preschools.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: From MSF and ECDA: anchor and partner operators who receive significant fiscal funding and preferential allocation to Housing and Development Board (HDB) sites with much lower rent.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: From MOE: kindergartens operating with the full backing of the national Budget, no binding constraint of rental costs, and a compelling competitive advantage – an implicit pathway into the affiliated primary school.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: As one operator told me: "Even zero rent also cannot survive." The direction of travel is clear: the "middle tier" of independent preschools is shrinking.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: But the method of direct operator subsidies used to achieve them has inadvertently created a deeply distorted market.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: The unfairness comes from the way subsidies are given.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: The first is the parent-level subsidy, which many parents will know.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: The Basic Childcare Subsidy provides a transparent and fair offset of $150 to $300 per month for any citizen child in an ECDA-licensed centre.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: But the second far more opaque category of operator-level subsidy is largely implemented through direct fiscal transfers.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: On the MSF side, this is only available to AOPs and POPs.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: On the MK side, this comes directly from the MOE national Budget.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: This is a direct transfer to these chosen Government-supported operators, and no one else.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: For independent operators, this trap has three walls.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: They face dwindling enrollment due to the breakneck expansion of AOPs and MKs, which use unequal fiscal grants to offer lower fees.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Simultaneously, these state-backed centres create a net talent drain by offering higher salaries, leaving independents to struggle with rising rental costs and a fight for survival.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Some say, "Join the Partner Operator scheme", as this is the intended way for private operators to enter the Government-supported umbrella.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: For many, this is a difficult choice: (a) the consortium requirement means they must expose their books to one another.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: One lead holds the purse strings and counterparty risk is high; (b) the selection criteria is opaque – if rejected, ECDA provides no reason and no feedback; (c) there is commercial lock-in: once fees are capped under the POP scheme, exiting is near-impossible as parents will likely not accept a reversion to significantly higher fees.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: For many operators in HDB sites, the inability to sell their businesses is a frustrating obstacle.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Transfer of lease requires HDB and ECDA approval, but rejections are given without reasons.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: One operator's sale was blocked with the vague, one-sentence justification that the new owner could not "ensure the continuity of care and education," leaving them with no path of appeal.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: The only path left is to shut down.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Many private operators started with good intentions to provide a way of education for their kids, pouring their life savings and their passion into creating nurturing spaces.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Speaker, let me state plainly what many operators believe.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: They suspect the Government wants to nationalise the sector.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: They ask three questions and they deserve straight answers.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Question one: does the Government want standardised, cookie-cutter early education?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Many feel the push for AOPs and MKs penalises operators who offer unique models – small teacher-child ratios, project-based learning, Montessori, Reggio Emilia, faith-based schools – that do not fit the standard mold.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Question two: does the Government wish to nationalise this sector?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Because if the intention is not nationalisation, why are these features present: AOP share increasing, MK count increasing, share of children served by AOPs, POPs and MKs targeted to be 80% by 2025, and no articulated vision for the independent sector beyond its “managed-decline”.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Question three: is the Government's ideal outcome a kindergarten market dominated by MKs, with the pre-kindergarten market dominated by major AOPs?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: I ask the Ministry to clarify if any transitional provisions were made for private operators caught by this announcement.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: While I have great admiration for those who work in AOPs and MKs, which have good programs on science, technology, engineering and mathematics (STEM) and public speaking, we must acknowledge these systems’ flaws.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Furthermore, MSF’s top-down directives to include neurodiverse children create chaotic environments.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: The typical AOP setting, with its bright white lights, cluttered displays and high noise levels, is often unsuited for the neurodiverse, and in turn, diverts resources from neurotypical children who must learn in a more disrupted environment.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: MKs increasingly run a standardised programme as their principals focus on Primary 1 readiness and “school-ify” our young children.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: I do not blame them, if their key performance indicators are more for Primary 1 results over preschool creativity, the push for Primary 1 readiness will almost always win.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: But we should have the space to “let children be children”.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: The accelerated roll-out of MKs with priority Primary 1 admission, feeds parental anxiety and creates focus on academic readiness over holistic development.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: There is an immense cost placed upon our teachers, who are on the frontlines of a system breeding burnout.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: They navigate an unstable market, with centres shutting down left and right, and are increasingly pushed into "cookie-cutter" state-led models that kill their passion for teaching.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: They manage large kindergarten 2 classes of 25 children and find it hard to give individualised attention.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: They spend precious time dealing with paperwork and writing incident reports instead of teaching.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: And they operate in a “kiasi” culture, driven by conservative interpretations of ECDA circulars.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: This is a culture where pencils must be stored lying flat for safety, where operators are afraid to let children taste prata during cultural lessons.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: I am told by both teachers and operators that it is causing many teachers to burnout and leave the AOP system, often after bonuses are paid.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: While I do not have official data, the anecdotal attrition estimates shared with me are concerningly high.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: This brings us to the cost for parents: a severe diminution of choice.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: As independent operators close, parents lose access to the diversity that could offer a refuge from these systemic flaws.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Without transparency on operator-level subsidies, it is impossible to assess the true cost and efficiency of these schemes.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: In some estates like Punggol and Jurong West, multiple AOPs are clustered together in a small area, all "fighting for numbers", displaying what they in China call "involution" or "内卷": a zero-sum game of wasteful competition.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Their three policy goals – affordability, increasing educator salaries, and quality assurance – are rolled out via chosen operators.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: I will lay out a sector-wide reform without biasing towards particular operators.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: First, we must fund the child, not the school.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Instead of funnelling opaque grants to select operators, we can create a portable preschool voucher that bundles all public support into a transparent, per-child amount.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Parents can use it at any licensed centre.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: This empowers parents to choose a preschool that best fits their child's needs – be it PCF, Montessori, faith-based organisations, or play-based centres.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: It forces all schools, including state-backed giants, to compete fairly on quality, philosophy, service; without pre-determining the winner's business model.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: This principle should be expanded to all operators, not just AOPs.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: On fee control: the Government may fear subsidy capture – that operators will absorb the voucher without lowering fees.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: The surest way to keep fees in check is to keep the market open and contestable.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: A January 2024 study on childcare in Minnesota found that when you fund parents directly, the market finds a way to create more supply.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: They found that increased voucher funding led to more providers entering the market, an expansion of available slots, and only modest price increases.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: This is what a healthy responsive market looks like.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: It is diversity – and the capacity of all to scale – that gives a market supply-elasticity.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: A system where operators "cannot remain, cannot consolidate and cannot sell" would create inelasticity and potential future subsidy capture.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: This is not a leap into the unknown.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Portable funding across operators, transparent reference prices and quality assurance can coexist.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: By contrast, the current system is highly susceptible to subsidy capture – with chosen operators capturing massive unequal subsidies that may not reach parents as choice or quality improvements.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: With vouchers, parents can control where the money goes.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: This will fix the school-level market where subsidies distort operator competition.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Speaker, the Government’s instinct is to solve every preschool problem – from teacher pay to special needs – by leaning on its chosen operators.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Every preschool policy target begins to look for an operator-led solution.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: We can use voucher supplements to achieve these policy targets while preserving a contestable market.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: The higher the pay, the larger the supplement.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: We can enforce this transparently using Central Provident Fund data to verify wages and National Institute of Early Childhood Development standards to ensure teacher quality.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: It turns every operator into a potential partner in raising standards.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Instead of forcing top-down integration, we give every child with assessed needs a portable, ring-fenced voucher supplement, based on their assessed needs, such as specialised teachers, lower ratios, or sensory-friendly environments.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: This funding follows the child, empowering parents of neurodiverse children to choose centres with resources to provide proper support.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: It will also allow the emergence of specialised centres.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Some may point to Hong Kong, which once had a pure flat-rate voucher system, but moved away from it in 2017.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Among the reasons given for moving away were ineffectiveness for raising teacher pay, addressing special needs and helping low-income families.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: In my assessment, the Hong Kong system’s flaw lay more with the flat rate, than the voucher system itself.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: We can learn from this by using targeted funding supplements for these policy targets: lower-income families, special needs, teacher wages.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: I believe we must make access to these locations fair and contestable.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: This ensures the public subsidy on rent is passed on directly to parents as affordability." I propose two pilots.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: First, MSF and the Ministry of National Development to run a sector-wide, open tender for the next batch of preschool sites in new HDB estates.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Second, MOE to pilot this same open-tender model in a small number of primary schools, say, five initially, inviting all qualified operators to compete.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Does the Government want standardised, cookie-cutter early education?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Does the Government want to nationalise this sector?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Is the Government's ideal outcome an AOP to MK nationalised model?

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: To clarify ECDA's actions in October 2022 regarding the wage announcement timing and to commit to level-playing field policies going forward.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: This means dismantling the walls of the trap that operators find themselves in.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Allow them to consolidate by providing detailed POP selection criteria and right of appeal.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: At this juncture, enforcing an educational monoculture is exactly the wrong philosophy toward an uncertain world.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: I appeal to the Government's sense of fairness and to parents' lived experience: let us not allow this quiet extinction to continue.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: If we have five more years of this, I think there will be nothing left to save.

speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
text: Let us shift our focus from creating national champions to nurturing a vibrant and resilient preschool ecosystem for all our children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are committed to providing every child with a good start in life.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Preschools play an important part in supporting our children's development, while meeting parents' caregiving needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Over the past decade, preschool enrolment in Singapore has steadily increased.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We have enough full-day preschool places to accommodate every resident child aged three and above.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Government has no plans to nationalise preschool education.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We value a diverse preschool sector where private preschools offer niche programmes that meet different preferences and needs of parents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We intend to keep the market open so that parents can continue to have choices.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Our foremost objective, as rightly mentioned by Mr Tiong, has been to ensure accessibility, affordability as well as quality of our preschools for our parents' children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And we do this today through a mix of measures.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Second, on the demand end, we provide a suite of subsidies.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And third, to uplift overall sectorial standards which will not happen organically, we work with the sector to provide broad based support.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: On the supply side, we fund private operators on the AOP or POP schemes to ensure they keep within fee caps while investing in quality improvements.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To ensure that our AOPs and POPs maintain high standards of quality, operators go through a rigorous selection process, not one that is opaque as the Member suggested.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Criteria consider factors such as the applicants' track record in providing quality childcare services, financial sustainability and accessibility of centres and local preschool demand.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Applicants must also demonstrate commitment and ability to meet the AOP and POP scheme requirements, which includes the ability to provide affordable and quality preschool services and enhance, professional development and career prospects for early childhood professionals.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Tiong suggested removing direct operator grants and replacing them with a per child subsidy via preschool vouchers for families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Implementing a vouchers scheme alone may result in unintended consequences such as increases in preschool fees without corresponding improvements in accessibility or quality, as experiences in some countries have shown.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In Hong Kong, where the preschool voucher scheme was implemented in 2007, but eventually discontinued, it worsened in equity as affluent families utilised vouchers for extra educational programmes.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Similarly, in the United Kingdom, a nursery voucher programme implemented in 1996 was also discontinued shortly, because rather than improving quality and choice, it created unfair competition, reduced provider diversity and potentially harmed educational outcomes for young children.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: On the demand end, we adopt a comprehensive approach to preschool affordability by keeping fees for Government-supported preschools low, and providing both universal and means tested childcare subsidies to parents.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: The Government provides all Singaporean children with basic subsidies of up to $300 each for full day childcare as well as means tested additional subsidies for eligible families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: As a result of both fee caps, as well as subsidies, we have been able to effectively reduce out-of-pocket expenses, while ensuring access and choice of quality preschools for families.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Full day childcare expenses before means tested subsidies will be similar to what households pay for primary school and after school care fees combined in 2026.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Tiong has implied that the preschool voucher system would give parents more autonomy to choose a preschool that suits their children's needs best and allowing for a market mechanism to work.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: This incentive is already built into the nature of childcare subsidies which preschools receive based on the number of children enrolled.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Parents today are discerning when choosing preschools that best meet their child's needs and preferences, and this has promoted healthy competition among preschool operators and consequent improvements in quality.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: A third plank in our strategy is to work with the sector to provide broad based support to uplift sectorial standards.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Tiong suggested using targeted voucher supplements to advance national objectives such as raising teacher wages.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Salary increases must correspond with higher professional skills and contributions.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: A proposal to provide vouchers to preschools may not necessarily raise educators' salaries.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Without due consideration for skills development and safeguards, such a move may run the risk of fee escalation without corresponding increase in quality of teaching.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In contrast, the Government has continued to make significant sector-wide moves over the past decade to invest heavily in professional development, enhance career progression and improve working conditions of early childhood educators.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: And one such example is the setting up of the National Institute of Early Childhood Development in 2019.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Tiong suggested using vouchers to advance support for children with special needs.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: On tenders for HDB and primary school sites, HDB sites are allocated to Government-supported preschools to avail affordable preschool services to residents soon after they move in.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Nevertheless, I want to assure him that there are HDB sites open to all operators to bid competitively for, even as ECDA works with HDB to ensure that there are sufficient sites allocated for affordable preschool places today.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Mr Tiong asks about preschool salary enhancements in 2022.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: To give better context, ECDA has been working with AOPs and POPs to raise salaries and deepen professionalisation since 2016.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In 2022, we signalled salary increases, paced over two years to maintain competitiveness relative to the broader labour market.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: Before the 2022 announcement, salaries for early childhood educators in Government supported preschools had already increased by 20% on average since 2018.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: I can say so because I think about this every day when I send my five-year-old son to preschool in the mornings.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: In 2019, we made a decisive move to expand Government supported preschool places to cater to 80% of preschoolers, so more Singaporean families can benefit from good access to affordable and quality preschools by the end of this year.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We are getting there, but our work is not done.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
text: We will continue to evolve our policies to improve access to affordable and quality preschools across the sector – so that every child can have a good start in life.
